text.p: Moises Alou had four hits and four RBI and Charles Johnson also drove in four runs to lead an 18-hit attack as the Florida Marlins crushed the Pittsburgh Pirates 12-3 Wednesday for their fourth straight win.
Edgar Renteria had three hits and scored twice, while Bobby Bonilla had two hits and an RBI and scored three times for Florida, which has won eight of its last nine games.

Florida starter Kevin Brown (10-8) contributed to the offensive explosion with two hits, and won for the first time in four starts. He held the Pirates to one run and six hits in seven innings with a walk and nine strikeouts, and said his main problem was not relaxing with the big lead.
"Nights like this are a nice problem to have," Brown said. "Even with that kind of lead you can't relax. It's not the approach to take. You've got to stay focused when you get that kind of lead."

The first seven batters reached safely in the top of the first against Pittsburgh starter Esteban Loiaza (8-8) as the Marlins grabbed a 4-0 lead. They added four more runs in the second and led 11-0 by the fifth.
Johnson hit a two-run homer in the second and a two-run double in the third and Alou added a solo shot in the fifth.

Every starter collected at least one hit for Florida, which remained 4 1/2 games behind first-place Atlanta in the National League East and increased its lead over the Mets to three games in the wild card race.
In Philadelphia, Mike Lieberthal's three-run homer capped a four-run first inning as the Phillies defeated the Houston Astros 6-4 for their seventh win in nine games.
Ramon Garcia (4-8) took the loss. He allowed five runs -- only one earned -- and nine hits in four-plus innings for the Astros, who have lost three straight.
Rookie Garrett Stephenson (6-5) allowed four runs and nine hits over seven innings, improving to 4-1 in his last five starts. Ricky Bottalico struck out two in a perfect ninth for his 21st save.
Scott Rolen and Tony Barron also homered for the Phillies.
Despite having the worst record in the majors, the Phillies have won four of seven from the Astros, who are five games ahead of second-place Pittsburgh in the N.L. Central.
In Montreal, Henry Rodriguez belted a three-run homer in the fifth and the Expos bullpen tossed 3 1/3 scoreless innings for a 7-3 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Montreal scored four times in the fifth against Chan Ho Park (10-6). Park had won his previous five starts.
Dustin Hermanson (6-5) allowed three runs and five hits over 5 2/3 innings to win his second straight start. Marc Valdes and Dave Veres went the rest of the way.
The Dodgers' third loss in four games dropped them 2 1/2 games behind first-place San Francisco in the N.L. West.

In Chicago, Pat Rapp worked 5 2/3 innings in his return from the disabled list and Mark Lewis homered and drove in the go-ahead run in the fifth as the San Francisco Giants won their fourth straight, 7-4 over the Cubs.

Rapp (5-6), making his second start as a Giant, allowed three runs and six hits with two walks and a strikeout. He was acquired from the Marlins on July 18 and suffered an abdominal strain in his first outing a day later. Rapp had lost his last four decisions.
San Francisco has won seven of its last 10 games.

In New York, rookie John Thomson tossed a four-hitter for his first major-league shutout and Andres Galarraga had three hits in his first game back from a three-game suspension as the Colorado Rockies blanked the Mets 4-0.
Thomson (4-6) scattered four singles and three walks. He struck out just two but threw 72 of 106 pitches for strikes.

Galarraga, who served a three-game suspension for charging the mound in a May 31 game, singled in the fifth, seventh and eighth. Ellis Burks added a solo homer for Colorado, which has won two in a row after dropping three straight.
Mets starter Dave Mlicki (5-8) allowed three runs and seven hits over six innings.

In Atlanta, pinch-hitter Danny Bautista's leadoff homer in the bottom of the ninth lifted the Braves to a 4-3 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals, who lost their fourth straight and eighth in nine games.
Trailing 3-1 in the sixth, the Braves rallied for three straight two-out hits. Fred McGriff tied it with a two-run double down the right-field line.

In Cincinnati, Craig Shipley ignited a three-run seventh with an RBI double and Ken Caminiti homered and drove in three runs as the San Diego Padres ended their three-game losing streak with a 6-3 victory over the Reds.
The Reds scored twice in the sixth for a 3-3 tie, but San Diego answered with three runs in the seventh off reliever Stan Belinda (1-3).
Joey Hamilton (10-3) won his sixth straight. Trevor Hoffman fanned two in a scoreless ninth for his 26th save in 32 opportunities.
